h1: PLAAI Prime Hotel Rayong — a modern-design city hotel that's a three-minute walk to the mall in central Rayong
intro: If you're coming to Rayong but not planning to sleep on Koh Samet every night — you're here to work, attend meetings, pass through, or just want a city base that's easy to get around with good-looking rooms — PLAAI Prime Hotel Rayong (formerly D Varee Diva Central Rayong) is a name guests bring up often · it's a 4-star city hotel on Sukhumvit Road in Noen Phra, just a 3 min walk to Passione Shopping Destination and Dr. Sarot Market · what wins the most praise is the modern room design, the semi-open bathroom with a bathtub, and the wide breakfast spread — though some reviews note the building is starting to show its age in places · from about ฿1,100/night · scored 9.2 from 413 reviews on Trip.com

body.html: Overview — who PLAAI Prime Rayong is for · Most people picture Rayong as beaches, Koh Samet and Mae Ramphueng Beach, but the town of Rayong itself is an industrial and commercial hub with people coming and going all year round — workers at the industrial estates, people in for conferences and seminars, and travellers stopping over before moving on · PLAAI Prime Hotel Rayong was built for exactly this crowd — a 4-star city hotel that originally opened as D Varee Diva Central Rayong before moving to operate under the PLAAI Hotels Group brand · what sets it apart from the average city hotel is how it positions itself as a design hotel that looks more modern than its price tag, with nicely styled rooms, bathtubs, and a location you can genuinely walk to the mall from · from real guest reviews, the people it suits best are business travellers, couples who want a good-looking room on a manageable budget, small families stopping in town before heading to the coast, and anyone driving through Rayong who wants a central base where food is easy to find · if your plan is to fall asleep to the sound of waves on the beach every night, though, this may not be the answer — you'd want to look at the Mae Ramphueng Beach side or cross over to Koh Samet instead

Location and getting around · This is PLAAI Prime's number-one selling point, no question · the hotel sits at 590 Sukhumvit Road, Noen Phra subdistrict, Mueang Rayong district, the main artery of the town · the thing reviews mention most is that it's only about a 3 min walk to Passione Shopping Destination, which pulls restaurants, a supermarket, coffee shops and stores together in one place — you can head out for dinner or shopping without calling a car · nearby there's also Dr. Sarot Market, about a 9 min walk, for anyone after local food and souvenirs · the Star IT Center mall is around 2.4 km away, a few minutes by car · longer trips are still manageable too: Mae Ramphueng Beach is about 17 km away (roughly a 25 min drive), Ban Phe pier for crossing to Koh Samet is a similar distance, and U-Tapao Airport (UTP) is about 40 km away, roughly a 45–50 min drive · driving down from Bangkok takes around 2.5–3 hr depending on traffic · one small note: the hotel sits right on Sukhumvit Road where traffic runs constantly, so rooms facing the street may catch some road noise — but in terms of convenience the location is a big advantage

"We chose this place because you can just walk to Passione — grab dinner and stroll back, no problem. The room was much nicer than I expected, with a bathtub too. For this price in central Rayong it's incredibly good value."

Room types and decor · PLAAI Prime has around 79 rooms in a contemporary style with an easy-on-the-eye palette — they look cleaner and more modern than the usual city hotel at the same price · it starts with the Deluxe Room, around 30 sqm, which, even as the entry-level room, is nicely laid out with a work desk, a city view, and the detail many people love: a semi-open bathroom with a freestanding bathtub and rain shower · step up to the Studio Suite with Pool View, around 42 sqm, which looks out over the pool and suits anyone who wants extra lounge space · there's a Family Room with a king bed plus a bunk bed for families travelling with kids · and the largest is the PLAAI Prime Suite One Bedroom, around 69 sqm, for anyone wanting an extra-spacious room · every room has air-conditioning, a 40-inch flat-screen TV, a minibar, a tea-and-coffee set, a safe, blackout curtains and free Wi-Fi · a lot of reviews agree that the beds are very comfortable, the rooms are well designed, and the bathtub is a detail that makes the place feel special beyond its price · but to be straight about it, some reviewers note the building is starting to age, with curtains or towels in certain rooms looking worn, and a few reviews ran into a leaking bathtub or pieces of furniture that aren't fresh — worth asking for a renovated room when you book

Facilities and the pool · The highlight people talk about is the outdoor pool, which many reviews say is kept clean, with clear water and good sun all day — perfect for a cooling soak after walking around town · some listings note it's a saltwater pool, gentler on the skin than a standard chlorine one · downstairs there's a gym for anyone who wants to work out, though some reviews note a few machines are getting old and could use an upgrade · there's also a restaurant serving Thai and international food, a bar, a café, meeting and seminar rooms, a business centre, room service and free parking · for anyone here to work or take online meetings, the in-room desk and Wi-Fi that reaches throughout the building both get praise · to be honest, the pool and gym here are city-hotel sized, not beachfront-resort scale, but in terms of how complete and clean they are, it's done well for this price point · kids stay free under the hotel's policy, which is a plus for families

Food and the bar · Breakfast is another star here · a lot of reviews praise the varied and tasty breakfast, with Thai, Asian and Western options plus hot dishes made to order, in a comfortable dining room · many use the phrase "absolutely delicious breakfast" in their English reviews · but for balance, some note that during the busy morning rush certain options run out quickly or the eggs arrive lukewarm — something you'll find at any hotel with a packed buffet at peak times · for other meals, the location helps a lot, because a walk to Passione or Dr. Sarot Market turns up restaurants and local food everywhere, so many people choose to eat out rather than dine in for every meal · there's a restaurant serving Thai and international food for lunch and dinner, and a bar-café for an evening drink · overall PLAAI Prime does well on food when it comes to breakfast, with everything else being a nice-to-have that leans on the city location as an advantage

Service · Service is a consistent strong point in the real reviews · several front-desk staff get singled out as friendly, attentive and bilingual, helping with restaurant recommendations, calling cars and sorting out various things well · on Trip.com the service category sits at around 9.1, which is high for a city hotel at this level · TripAdvisor also has plenty of reviews specifically praising the front-desk team's professionalism · but to be straight about it, some say service isn't equally consistent at every moment, especially when the hotel is full or has a seminar group checked in · overall, service is still a strength that leaves guests impressed and brings them back

What real reviews say (the good and the gripes) · Pulling from Trip.com, Agoda and TripAdvisor, the picture lines up fairly consistently · On the praise side: a central location a 3 min walk to Passione mall, rooms that look stylish and modern beyond their price, the bathtub in the semi-open bathroom, very comfortable beds, a varied and tasty breakfast, friendly bilingual staff, and a clean pool with good sun · On the watch-out side: the thing mentioned most is that the building is starting to age — some reviews say the hotel is "past its best," with curtains, towels and certain pieces of furniture looking less than fresh, and a few rooms had a leaking bathtub · after that come a few gym machines that could use an upgrade, road noise from Sukhumvit Road in street-facing rooms, and a peak-time breakfast where some items run out fast or arrive lukewarm · these gripes are things you can manage by choosing the right room and setting expectations properly, rather than big problems that keep people away — and the 9.2 from 413 reviews reflects that most guests are happy overall

"Clean room, soft bed, lovely staff who recommended restaurants around town. My only gripe was the curtains and towels looking a bit worn, and the street-facing room caught some traffic noise — next time I'll ask for one on the inside instead."

Price and value comparison · The Deluxe Room's starting price is around ฿1,100/night in the normal range (about USD 34 as shown on Trip.com), climbing to roughly ฿2,000–2,800+ during high season or long weekends · larger rooms like the Studio Suite Pool View and the PLAAI Prime Suite One Bedroom run from around ฿1,800 up to roughly ฿3,500+ depending on size and timing · compared with other city hotels in Rayong — like Star Convention Hotel, which leans on roomy, budget-friendly rooms — PLAAI Prime feels good value when it comes to design and a premium feel — you get a stylish room, a bathtub, and a walk-to-the-mall location at a price that's still manageable · if you care about the room atmosphere and getting good photos, this delivers value the average city hotel can't · but if you're after the most room space per baht or a long stay with several people, you may want to compare it against the larger suites at other hotels in town too

What to know before you book · A few things make the stay go more smoothly · one, if you're sensitive to noise, specify at booking that you want an inside room not facing Sukhumvit Road, because traffic runs along it constantly · two, since the building is starting to age, ask for a renovated room, and if the bathtub matters to you, flag it in advance to avoid a room that might have a leak · three, if your main goal is the beach, plan for transport, since it's about a 25 min drive to Mae Ramphueng Beach · four, over long weekends and Rayong's tourist season rooms fill fast and prices climb, so book ahead and compare across platforms · five, go with free cancellation if your plans aren't firm yet, since prices often shift with the timing · six, use Passione as your base for food and an evening bite — it'll save you both time and travel costs

The verdict · From everything in the real reviews, PLAAI Prime Hotel Rayong (formerly D Varee Diva Central Rayong) is the best fit for anyone who wants a city hotel in Rayong with a stylish modern room, a bathtub, and a walk to the mall at a manageable price — great for work trips, conferences, pass-throughs, couples, and small families using the town as a base before heading to the coast · the 3 min walk to Passione, the room design that looks more premium than the price, the varied breakfast, and the attentive service make it a solid choice in central Rayong · but if you're after beachfront calm or want a brand-new room that's flawless in every corner, this may not be the answer, since it's a city hotel with a building that's starting to age and a drive still ahead to the sea · overall, among Rayong's city hotels, PLAAI Prime is one of the most balanced picks for looks, convenience and value — fitting for the 9.2 from 413 reviews guests have given it

faq.q: What was PLAAI Prime Hotel Rayong formerly called, and where is it?
faq.a: PLAAI Prime Hotel Rayong originally opened as D Varee Diva Central Rayong and is now operated under the PLAAI Hotels Group brand · it's located at 590 Sukhumvit Road, Noen Phra subdistrict, Mueang Rayong district in central Rayong · just about a 3 min walk to Passione Shopping Destination and about 9 min to Dr. Sarot Market

faq.q: What's the starting price at PLAAI Prime Rayong, and what room types are there?
faq.a: From about ฿1,100/night for a Deluxe Room of around 30 sqm in the normal range · above that there's the Studio Suite Pool View (~42 sqm), the Family Room (king bed + bunk bed) and the PLAAI Prime Suite One Bedroom (~69 sqm) · prices climb over long weekends, so compare a few platforms before booking

faq.q: Who is PLAAI Prime Hotel Rayong best for?
faq.a: A great fit for people here to work, attend conferences or pass through, plus couples and small families who want a city hotel in Rayong with a stylish room, a bathtub, and a walk to the mall · not ideal for anyone set on sleeping by the sea every night, since it's a city hotel about 17 km from Mae Ramphueng Beach, with a drive ahead

faq.q: Does the hotel have a pool, gym and bathtub?
faq.a: Yes · the hotel has a clean outdoor pool with good sun, a gym, a restaurant, a bar, a café and free parking · a standout is that many rooms have a semi-open bathroom with a freestanding bathtub and rain shower · the watch-out is that a few gym machines are getting old, per reviews

faq.q: What are the rooms and the building like?
faq.a: The praise goes to stylish modern rooms, comfortable beds, cleanliness and a bathtub · but some reviews note the building is starting to age, with curtains, towels and certain furniture looking less than fresh, and a few rooms had a leaking bathtub · we'd suggest asking for a renovated room when you book
